about: The Govern catalog (doc 94): what an organisation needs across governance, people, process and technology, tiered basic (the minimum every organisation must have), standard (good practice for a regulated or mid-size organisation) and advanced (the highest level worth reaching). Generic and in SecuRAX's own words; no organisation's data. impact 1-5 = how much risk it removes. cost: fixed = Rs lakh per year (licence + service; first-year one-off costs are folded in); per_endpoint / per_user = Rs per year per unit. All costs are indicative bands for India, October 2026, from public price and salary surveys (doc 94 lists them): always confirm with three quotes.

tiers.basic: Minimum basic: what any organisation must have to be defensible
tiers.standard: Standard: good practice for a regulated or mid-size organisation
tiers.advanced: Highest possible: leading practice, worth it once the rest is solid

capabilities.name: Information security policy and standards
capabilities.why: Without approved rules, nobody can be held to them and no audit can pass
capabilities.how: Adopt the template policy, tailor it, get Board or committee approval, review yearly

capabilities.name: Security governance: CISO, steering committee, RACI
capabilities.why: Security decisions need an owner with authority and a forum that meets
capabilities.how: Name the CISO, form a steering committee that meets quarterly, publish a RACI

capabilities.name: Risk management framework and risk register
capabilities.why: Money and time go to the biggest risks only when risks are named, scored and owned
capabilities.how: Use ISO 31000 / 27005 style scoring, keep the register template, review monthly

capabilities.name: KPIs, KRIs and Board reporting
capabilities.why: What the Board cannot see, it cannot fund or back
capabilities.how: One page each quarter: posture, top risks, what changed, what we need

capabilities.name: Data protection programme (DPDP Act)
capabilities.why: Personal data carries legal duties and penalties
capabilities.how: Data map, notices and consent, rights handling, breach process, processor contracts; the DPDP Rules were notified in November 2025 and most duties apply from about May 2027 (check the Gazette)

capabilities.name: Third-party and vendor risk management
capabilities.why: Many breaches arrive through suppliers
capabilities.how: Tier vendors by access and data, questionnaire, contract clauses, yearly review

capabilities.name: ISO 27001 ISMS (certified)
capabilities.why: An audited management system keeps controls alive year after year
capabilities.how: Scope, gap assessment, statement of applicability, internal audit, certification

capabilities.name: ISO 22301 business continuity (certified)
capabilities.why: Recovery that is planned and tested, not hoped for
capabilities.how: Business impact analysis, recovery strategies, plans, exercises, certification

capabilities.name: GRC platform
capabilities.why: Policies, risks, audits and exceptions in one place, with evidence
capabilities.how: Start with the registers in this pack; move to a platform once they are in use; the open-source route (eramba, CISO Assistant) costs about Rs 2.5-5 lakh a year

capabilities.name: Cyber risk insurance
capabilities.why: Transfers the residual financial impact of a major incident
capabilities.how: Size cover to a realistic worst case; insurers reward the basics being in place; premiums run about 0.5-2.5% of the sum insured a year

capabilities.name: AI governance and model risk
capabilities.why: AI systems bring new data, accuracy and attack risks
capabilities.how: Inventory of AI use, approval rules, testing before use, human in command; RBI's FREE-AI framework (August 2025) expects a Board-approved AI policy, so a bank should treat this as standard

capabilities.name: A core security team, sized to the organisation
capabilities.why: Tools without people to run them are money spent for nothing
capabilities.how: Size with ./securax govern team; hire leads first; consultants may fill gaps with knowledge transfer; salaries are costed in  ./securax govern team

capabilities.name: Security awareness and phishing simulation
capabilities.why: Most attacks start with a person being tricked
capabilities.how: Monthly short lessons, quarterly phishing tests, extra help for those who click

capabilities.name: Technical training and certification for the team
capabilities.why: Skills decay fast in security; trained staff need fewer consultants
capabilities.how: A training plan per role, one certification per person per year, budget per head

capabilities.name: Consultant knowledge-transfer plan
capabilities.why: Consultants should leave capability behind, not dependence
capabilities.how: Year 1 consultants lead and teach; year 2 the internal team leads

capabilities.name: Cyber range exercises
capabilities.why: Teams that have practised respond faster and with fewer mistakes
capabilities.how: Quarterly live-fire exercises; SecuRAX's own range is a free start (./securax exercise)

capabilities.name: Asset and data inventory
capabilities.why: You cannot protect what you do not know you have
capabilities.how: Inventory template: every system, its owner, its data, its exposure; reconcile monthly

capabilities.name: Criticality and sensitivity classification
capabilities.why: Priorities follow from what is critical and what is sensitive
capabilities.how: Rate each asset for criticality and data sensitivity (1-4 each); the product sets its priority

capabilities.name: Vulnerability management with closure SLAs
capabilities.why: Known, unfixed weaknesses are how most attackers get in
capabilities.how: Scan, rate, assign, fix within SLA, re-test before closing; report repeat findings

capabilities.name: Patch management
capabilities.why: Most exploited weaknesses already have a patch
capabilities.how: Monthly cycle, emergency path for exploited flaws (CISA KEV), coverage report

capabilities.name: Change and exception management
capabilities.why: Unreviewed changes and permanent 'temporary' exceptions open quiet holes
capabilities.how: Risk-assess every change; every exception has an owner, an end date and a compensating control; free only where an ITSM tool exists, otherwise about Rs 15-35 lakh a year

capabilities.name: Access reviews and joiner-mover-leaver
capabilities.why: Leftover access is a door left open
capabilities.how: Quarterly access review for critical systems; same-day removal at exit

capabilities.name: Incident response plan and crisis management plan
capabilities.why: A written, practised plan turns a crisis into a procedure, and meets reporting clocks (CERT-In: 6 hours)
capabilities.how: Roles, severity levels, playbooks, regulator clocks, contact tree; tabletop twice a year; include the DPDP breach notice to the Data Protection Board; an IR retainer adds about Rs 12-85 lakh a year

capabilities.name: Backups that are tested and kept offline
capabilities.why: The difference between a bad day and a business-ending ransomware attack
capabilities.how: 3-2-1-1-0: an offline copy, encrypted, and a restore test every quarter

capabilities.name: Secure development and API security checklist
capabilities.why: Fixing a flaw before go-live costs a fraction of fixing it after
capabilities.how: Security requirements, threat modelling, the API checklist and tests before every release

capabilities.name: Vendor scorecards and SLA reviews
capabilities.why: Paying for tools and services that are not used or not delivered is pure loss
capabilities.how: Quarterly scorecard per vendor: deliverables, SLAs, features enabled, issues

capabilities.name: BCP / DR drills and tabletop exercises
capabilities.why: A recovery never tested will fail when needed
capabilities.how: Yearly DR switch-over; tabletop twice a year with management

capabilities.name: Continuous threat exposure management
capabilities.why: Moves from yearly snapshots to a continuously updated view of exposure
capabilities.how: Scope, discover, prioritise, validate, mobilise, in monthly cycles

capabilities.name: Next-generation firewalls (perimeter and data centre)
capabilities.why: The first filter for everything coming in and going out
capabilities.how: Default deny, reviewed rules, logs to the SIEM, yearly rule clean-up

capabilities.name: Email security (anti-phishing, sandboxing, DMARC)
capabilities.why: Email is the most common way in
capabilities.how: Gateway or cloud filter, attachment sandbox, SPF/DKIM/DMARC at reject

capabilities.name: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) with antivirus
capabilities.why: Catches and stops attacks on laptops and servers, including ransomware
capabilities.how: Every endpoint and server covered, blocking mode on, alerts to the SOC

capabilities.name: Multi-factor authentication everywhere that matters
capabilities.why: Stops most account take-over from stolen passwords
capabilities.how: Remote access, email, admin and critical apps first; phishing-resistant for admins

capabilities.name: Vulnerability scanning
capabilities.why: Finds the weaknesses before attackers do
capabilities.how: Authenticated scans monthly; internet-facing weekly; results feed the SLA process

capabilities.name: Central log collection and retention
capabilities.why: No logs, no detection and no investigation; regulators expect 180 days in India
capabilities.how: Collect from firewalls, identity, endpoints and critical apps; keep 180 days or more

capabilities.name: Encryption of devices, databases and backups
capabilities.why: A lost laptop or stolen backup stays unreadable
capabilities.how: Full-disk on laptops, database and backup encryption, keys managed apart from data; payment and signing keys need HSMs at extra cost (an HA pair plus DR is about Rs 1-2 crore one-off)

capabilities.name: Web application firewall
capabilities.why: Shields web applications from common attacks while fixes are made
capabilities.how: In front of every internet-facing app, blocking mode after a learning period

capabilities.name: Anti-DDoS protection
capabilities.why: Keeps online services up during a traffic flood
capabilities.how: Upstream (ISP or cloud) scrubbing plus on-premise detection

capabilities.name: DNS security
capabilities.why: Blocks calls to malicious sites and command-and-control
capabilities.how: Protective DNS for all users; DNSSEC on own domains

capabilities.name: Network access control
capabilities.why: Only known, healthy devices reach the network
capabilities.how: Start with critical segments; posture checks; guest isolation

capabilities.name: Mobile device management
capabilities.why: Lost phones and tablets can be wiped; company data stays separate
capabilities.how: Enrol every company device; containers for personal devices

capabilities.name: Privileged access management
capabilities.why: Admin accounts are what attackers want most
capabilities.how: Vault admin passwords, just-in-time access, recorded sessions

capabilities.name: Identity governance (IAM / IGA)
capabilities.why: The right access for the right people, reviewed and removed on time
capabilities.how: One identity source, role-based access, automated joiner-mover-leaver

capabilities.name: Active Directory security assessment and hardening
capabilities.why: Whoever controls the directory controls the organisation
capabilities.how: Assessment, tiered admin model, remove stale and over-privileged accounts, monitor; a commercial identity-threat tool adds about Rs 40 lakh-1.1 crore a year where Microsoft 365 E5 is not owned

capabilities.name: SIEM (security monitoring platform)
capabilities.why: Turns logs into detections the team can act on
capabilities.how: Use cases mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, tuned monthly; licence by log volume

capabilities.name: Security operations centre (24x7, in-house or managed)
capabilities.why: Someone must be watching and able to respond at 3 am
capabilities.how: Managed SOC first, in-house later if scale justifies it; clear SLAs and runbooks; the band is for managed or hybrid: an in-house 24x7 SOC costs about Rs 2.5-4 crore a year

capabilities.name: Application security testing (SAST / DAST / code review)
capabilities.why: Finds flaws in your own software before release
capabilities.how: In the build pipeline; release blocked on critical findings

capabilities.name: Attack surface management
capabilities.why: Finds forgotten internet-facing systems before attackers do
capabilities.how: Continuous external discovery; every new finding gets an owner

capabilities.name: Threat intelligence
capabilities.why: Knowing what is being used against your sector right now
capabilities.how: Sector feeds (CERT-In, CSIRT-Fin), indicators into SIEM and blocking

capabilities.name: Data loss prevention
capabilities.why: Stops sensitive data leaving by email, web or USB
capabilities.how: Start in monitor mode on the most sensitive data; block once tuned

capabilities.name: Data discovery and classification tool
capabilities.why: Finds where sensitive data really is
capabilities.how: Scan file shares, databases and cloud; label; feed DLP

capabilities.name: Zero trust network access
capabilities.why: Every user and device proves itself for each application; no flat network
capabilities.how: Replace VPN app by app, starting with the most sensitive; start with third-party and admin users

capabilities.name: Network detection and response
capabilities.why: Sees attackers moving inside the network
capabilities.how: Sensors at key segments; alerts to the SOC

capabilities.name: SOAR (automated response)
capabilities.why: Responds in seconds to the alerts that do not need a human
capabilities.how: Automate the top 10 playbooks first

capabilities.name: User and entity behaviour analytics / XDR
capabilities.why: Spots insiders and stolen accounts by unusual behaviour
capabilities.how: Baseline behaviour; alert on strong deviations

capabilities.name: Breach and attack simulation
capabilities.why: Proves the controls work, instead of assuming
capabilities.how: Weekly safe simulations; gaps go into the vulnerability process

capabilities.name: Deception (honeypots and decoys)
capabilities.why: Any touch on a decoy is an intruder: very early, very reliable warning
capabilities.how: Decoys in the DMZ and key internal segments

capabilities.name: API security platform
capabilities.why: APIs carry the data; they are the main target of modern attacks
capabilities.how: Discover every API, test against the checklist, protect at runtime

capabilities.name: Bot mitigation and runtime app protection (RASP)
capabilities.why: Stops credential stuffing and automated fraud on digital channels
capabilities.how: In front of login and payment journeys first

capabilities.name: Database activity monitoring and data masking
capabilities.why: Watches who reads sensitive data; test systems get masked data
capabilities.how: Critical databases first; masking for every non-production copy

capabilities.name: Digital rights management
capabilities.why: Sensitive documents stay protected after they are shared
capabilities.how: For Board, legal and strategy documents first

capabilities.name: Digital forensics capability
capabilities.why: Evidence that holds up, and the real cause of an incident
capabilities.how: Retainer with a forensics firm plus a basic in-house kit (./securax respond)

capabilities.name: Quantum-safe cryptography readiness
capabilities.why: Data stolen today could be decrypted later
capabilities.how: Inventory where cryptography is used; prefer hybrid post-quantum key exchange; build a cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM) and ask every vendor for its PQC roadmap

roles.name: CISO / Head of Information Security
roles.skills: Strategy, risk, Board reporting, regulation, budget
roles.certs: CISSP or CISM; CISO-level BFSI experience; for an RBI-regulated entity: senior rank (GM or equivalent), reports to an ED or equivalent and not to the Head of IT, no business targets, a minimum term (RBI IT governance directions, 2023)

roles.name: GRC lead
roles.skills: Policy, risk assessment, audits, vendor risk, regulatory mapping
roles.certs: CISM, CRISC, CISA; ISO 27001 Lead Auditor

roles.name: GRC analyst
roles.skills: Risk registers, evidence, internal audit, documentation

roles.name: Security architect
roles.skills: Secure design, cloud, identity, zero trust, API security

roles.name: Security testing lead
roles.skills: VAPT, red teaming, code review, API security, vendor oversight

roles.name: Security tester / AppSec engineer
roles.skills: Web, mobile and API testing, SAST/DAST, vulnerability management
roles.certs: OSCP, GWAPT, OSWE (hands-on first); CEH is tender-friendly but weaker proof of skill

roles.name: Security engineering / tooling lead
roles.skills: EDR, DLP, PAM, NAC, tool strategy and integration

roles.name: SOC manager
roles.skills: SOC operations, detection engineering, KPIs, threat hunting
roles.certs: GCIA, GCIH, or a SIEM certification such as SC-200 or Splunk

roles.name: SOC analyst L1
roles.certs: Security+, SC-200 or a SIEM certification

roles.name: Incident response lead
roles.skills: IR, DFIR, crisis management, regulator reporting

roles.name: Resilience (BCP/DR) lead
roles.certs: CBCP or BCI CBCI, ISO 22301 Lead Implementer

sources: Ready reckoner research, October 2026: vendor pages, Indian reseller and analyst price guides, RBI, CERT-In and MeitY texts; one source list per item in governance/reckoner/*.json
Salaries: public Indian salary surveys, 2026 (weekday.works, taggd.in, amityonline.com and others); ranges, not quotes
Managed SOC and SIEM: Indian provider estimates (mid-market SIEM licence about Rs 40-80 lakh a year; in-house 24x7 SOC Rs 2-4 crore a year); managed SOC a few lakh to Rs 15-20 lakh a month
EDR: Indian reseller ranges of about Rs 2,200-5,000 per endpoint per year (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender)
